assertions.control: deep equality with the decoded control block
assertions.control_shape: structural facts, used where echoing the block would only make the corpus large
assertions.payload_len: byte length of the decoded payload

outcomes.accept: decodes to the given control block and payload
outcomes.reject: refused with the given error code
outcomes.incomplete: the datagrams end mid-message; a socket implementation surfaces this as a timeout or a closed peer

cases.name: control only
cases.why: the common case: an op with no payload

cases.name: control and a small payload
cases.why: one payload datagram

cases.name: payload spanning several datagrams
cases.why: 70400 bytes is past max_chunk, which is why the payload is chunked

cases.name: control block spanning several datagrams
cases.why: 232913 bytes, past SO_SNDBUF: the defect that forced chunking the control block too

cases.name: non-ascii control block
cases.why: 57 bytes for 37 characters: the length arithmetic counts bytes, and this is where that is proved

control.note: 日本語のテキスト認識

cases.name: prologue without an explicit protocol field
cases.why: protocol is optional on the wire; absent means the current version

cases.name: prologue announcing a future protocol version
cases.why: the one failure the version field exists to catch: refuse, do not serve it

cases.name: prologue missing payload_len
cases.why: the IDL marks it required; a default of zero hides a peer that forgot the payload

cases.name: prologue is not utf-8 json
cases.why: a peer speaking something else must be told, not guessed at

cases.name: prologue is a json array
cases.why: shape matters, not just parseability

cases.name: control block is not json
cases.why: the prologue was fine, the body is not

cases.name: control block is a json array
cases.why: a control block must be an object

cases.name: control_len of zero
cases.why: every message has a control block; zero means the peer is confused

cases.name: negative control_len
cases.why: a length must be a non-negative integer

cases.name: control_len is a boolean
cases.why: json true is an int in some languages; it is not a length

cases.name: control_len past max_control
cases.why: announced, not sent: refuse before allocating

cases.name: payload_len past max_payload
cases.why: same, for the payload ceiling

cases.name: a datagram larger than max_chunk
cases.why: the sender ignored the chunk limit; MSG_TRUNC catches it rather than silence

cases.name: more control bytes than announced
cases.why: the sender and the prologue disagree

cases.name: prologue larger than the prologue ceiling
cases.why: the first datagram is meant to be small and fixed-shape

cases.name: fewer control datagrams than announced
cases.why: a stalled or truncated sender; a socket surfaces this as a timeout or a close

cases.name: payload announced but never sent
cases.why: the classic half-sent message

cases.name: nothing at all
cases.why: an empty read means the peer closed
